newsitem.title: USA: Calif. foreclosures may be leveling off - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. foreclosures may be leveling off - report.

text.p: Foreclosure activity in California has leveled off and may be starting to recede, a real estate information service reported on Friday.

Lenders started foreclosure proceedings against 39,495 California homeowners during last year's fourth quarter, up 1.0 percent from 39,106 for the third quarter and up 4.9 percent from 37,648 for 1995's fourth quarter, according to DataQuick Information Systems.
The quarterly numbers peaked at 44,686 during last year's first quarter when lending institutions implemented stricter policies in their handling of mortgage delinquencies, it said.
While foreclosure activity is still on the rise in California's Central Valley, it declined significantly last quarter in several counties, DataQuick reported.
San Diego County experienced a 15.4 percent year-over-year decline. In Santa Clara County it was down 18.1 percent and in Orange County foreclosure activity was down 19.8 percent.

"With the current increase in home sales, these foreclosure properties will gradually become a smaller part of the market and will put less of a drag on home prices," Mike Ela, DataQuick's president, said in a statement.
DataQuick, a business unit of Conway, Ark.-based Acxiom Corp, monitors real estate activity nationwide.
